shots.narration: Why was a young man running barefoot through the streets of Rome?
As a boy, Abebe Bikila played gena, a traditional long distance hockey game.
Swedish coach Onni Niskanen noticed Abebe and began training him for the marathon.
At the 1960 Rome Olympics, Abebe won the marathon barefoot as Ethiopia's first gold medalist.
Emperor Haile Selassie awarded Abebe the Star of Ethiopia and promoted him to corporal.
Forty days before the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, Abebe underwent an appendectomy.
At the Tokyo Games, he became the first athlete to defend an Olympic marathon title.
A car accident on March 22, 1969, left Abebe paralysed from the neck down.
At a competition in Norway, he won the cross country sleigh riding event.
After Abebe died in Addis Ababa, Emperor Haile Selassie declared a national day of mourning.
